howToFill: One entry per query. The harness never edits this file; it reads it every time it scores.
benchmark: the lowest price you can find for a NEW unit of exactItem, as a single unit, from a store you would buy from.

benchmark.totalPrice: item price + shipping to you, BEFORE sales tax (tax depends on your state, not the store, so both sides leave it out). Or fill itemPrice and shipping and leave totalPrice null; the harness adds them.
benchmark.store: the store name as the site shows it (Best Buy, Walmart, Amazon). benchmark.checkedOn: YYYY-MM-DD. url and notes are optional.

acceptableTwins: null means not reviewed yet. [] means you reviewed it and no twin is acceptable. Otherwise a list of names (every word must appear in the listing name, e.g. "Soundcore Space One") or rules ({"all": ["space one"], "none": ["pro"]}).

exactItem.match decides which listing names count as the exact item: every 'all' entry must appear (a list means any one of them) and no 'none' term may. 'variant' pins a size, edition or generation: a title stating another one is not the item, and a title stating none is counted but marked 'variant unstated'. Terms with digits match ignoring spaces and punctuation ("wh-1000xm5" matches WH1000XM5); other terms match whole words. Edit these if an entry pins something you would not.
Shipping in your benchmark: use what a shopper with no membership pays (no Prime, Walmart+ or Target Circle 360), the same guest-tier assumption Pick's shipping figures use.
Re-score after editing: npx tsx eval/run.ts --replay latest (free, no API calls).
